source_lines.57: Assume full AC. In the standard solid torus $V=S^1\times D^2$, let $P_{2,1}$ be the oriented curve $s\mapsto(e^{4\pi i s},r e^{2\pi i s})$ on an interior parallel torus, where $0<r<1$. Let $K=T(2,3)$ be the right trefoil and use the companion embedding that matches the product meridian and longitude of $V$ to the positive meridian and preferred longitude of $K$. The outer torus of $X_{P_{2,1}}$ is incompressible, and $X_{P_{2,1}}$ is not a product $T^2\times[0,1]$ with its outer and inner tori as ends. The companion torus $T_c$ is essential; both pieces of $E_{P_{2,1}(K)}$ cut along $T_c$ are Seifert-fibered, while the whole satellite exterior is neither atoroidal nor Seifert-fibered. Every inclusion-minimal JSJ system has one torus ambient isotopic to $T_c$, and cutting along $T_c$ has the trefoil exterior as its outside component.

source_lines.82: 1.3 Fix a standard geometric basis a_i,b_i on the actual compact oriented genus-g surface with one boundary circle. Its existence follows by cutting a finite disk-and-handle model of the surface, not from an arbitrary homology basis. Put omega(a_i,b_j)=delta_ij. An annular Dehn twist about an embedded curve v acts by the transvection T_v(z)=z+omega(z,v)v, choosing the twist sign accordingly. This formula is proved by cutting each transverse arc at the annulus: the twisted arc acquires one oriented copy of its core. Curves representing a_i+a_j, b_i+b_j and a_i+b_j for i≠j are embedded band sums on distinct handles. The joining arc lies in the complement of the other standard handles; the band gives the indicated homology class. Thus these transvections and their inverses are actual boundary-fixed surface homeomorphisms (smooth diffeomorphisms in the smooth model). [F5, construct]
source_lines.86: 1.5 Taking u=a_i,v=b_j, i≠j, realizes the elementary block-GL operation a_j to a_j+a_i and b_i to b_i−b_j. Its powers realize arbitrary integral elementary additions. Euclidean elimination consequently realizes every block action (x,y) to (A x,A^−T y) for A in GL_g(Z). Likewise the a_i and a_i+a_j twists realize every symmetric upper shear, because the diagonal rank-one matrices and the identity (e_i+e_j)(e_i+e_j)^T−E_ii−E_jj=E_ij+E_ji generate all symmetric integral matrices; the b_i analogues realize every symmetric lower shear. source_lines.45: Let knots be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented S³ and let I=[0,1]. Let C_sm be their smooth concordance classes, where equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in S³×I. Let C_top be their locally flat topological concordance classes in that product. Let C_ex be their exotic-smooth concordance classes: equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W together with an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of pairs (W,∂W)≅(S³×I,S³×{0,1}) matching the endpoint knots. The annulus is oriented so that its boundary is −K₀ at the lower end and K₁ at the upper end, and it has product collars at both ends agreeing with the ambient boundary collars. For a nonzero integer n set R_n=Z[1/|n|]. Let C^{1/n} be the classes under equivalence witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W with boundary the two standard endpoint 3-spheres such that each boundary inclusion induces an isomorphism H_i(S³;R_n)→H_i(W;R_n) for every i. The annulus is oriented so that its boundary is −K₀ at the lower end and K₁ at the upper end, with product collars at both ends agreeing with the ambient boundary collars. A knot is pseudo-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold homeomorphic to B⁴, with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³. A knot is Z[1/|n|]-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold B with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³ and with H_i(B;R_n)≅H_i(B⁴;R_n) for every i; such a B is an R_n-homology 4-ball. These are sets of equivalence classes; this definition alone asserts no group structure.

This local complement recipe follows by taking the product normal2disk to a surface0handle or1handle: its complement adds respectively the normal meridian1handle or the2handle whose core crosses the band. The product collars identify the attaching pieces; no arbitrary embedded4ball is identified with the standard ball. The resulting complement deformation retracts onto a2complex with one vertex, one1cell and2g2cells. Name the positive normal meridian of its one1handle a. The local2handle at an oriented surface band identifies its endpoint meridians by transport through the band: its attaching relation is m_1 w m_2^−1 w^−1. To see the signs, take the boundary of a normal2disk and transport it along the band core; the two boundary ends of the resulting normal-annulus strip have opposite induced boundary orientations. Both endpoint meridians come from the same original disk and represent a in the one-generator1skeleton. Any winding of a knotted band only changes the transport word w, which is a power of a there. Thus the attaching word is a a^k a^−1 a^−k=1, for every band. Consequently pi1(N)=Z, and the same2complex is homotopy equivalent to a circle wedge2g spheres. source_lines.50: Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, let $F$ be a genus-$g$ Seifert surface, and let $(M,\gamma)$ be the balanced sutured manifold obtained by cutting the compact exterior of $K$ along $F$. For a surface-adapted admissible sutured Heegaard diagram, the generator correspondence between the top Alexander summand of the knot Floer complex and the sutured Floer disk-count module identifies their disk-count differentials. Under the hypotheses of a horizontal decomposition, the induced chain map realizes Ni's horizontal decomposition formula. For an essential separating product annulus with connected $R_+$ and $R_-$ whose decomposition has two balanced pieces, the induced chain map realizes Ni's product-annulus tensor formula. These assertions use the specified basepoint domains, periodic-domain admissibility, and exact characteristic-product-region hypotheses; they make no claim that generic Heegaard disk existence alone supplies the decomposition maps.

source_lines.51: Let P be an oriented pattern of winding n≠0 and K an oriented knot. If P(U) bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold B whose oriented boundary is identified with the standard oriented S³ and H_i(B;R_n)≅H_i(B⁴;R_n) for every i, then for every K the zero surgeries M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly R_n-homology cobordant. For the positive meridians determined by the supplied orientations, their images in the cobordism satisfy [mu_K]=n[mu_{P(K)}]; in particular they differ by a unit of R_n. This is a winding-unit meridian comparison, not a claim of literal equality for arbitrary winding. If P has strong winding number ±1 and P(U) is pseudo-slice (respectively locally flat topologically slice), then M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly (respectively topologically) homology cobordant through a 4-manifold whose fundamental group is normally generated by the image of the fundamental group of either boundary component. The category and closure hypotheses are separate and cannot be inferred from winding alone.
